newsitem.title: USA: USWC low sulphur diesel prices gain in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: USWC low sulphur diesel prices gain in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast low sulphur diesel prices were the lone gainers in quiet spot trade Wednesday, traders said, after Chevron reportedly bought large amounts of the distillate overnight.
Traders said the refiner needed to replace supplies because a crude unit at El Segundo remains in maintenance shutdown beyond its expected return.
The talk lifted low sulphur prices two cents a gallon in Los Angeles to 78/79 cents.
San Francisco material rose about three cents to 79/80 cents, traders said.
Spot trade remained thin, with traders leaving early for an industry conferance that is expected to dry up trade tomorrow.
Jet fuel prices, which rose amid shortages last week, saw offers ease 0.50 cents today to 80, as imports were reported en route to the west, traders said.
The arrival of jet fuel imports and the return of ARCO's 4,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) hydrocracker near Los Angeles, weighed on the West Coast distillate, traders said.
CARB diesel cargoes ranged between 85 and 87 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, flat from late Tuesday and off from a high last week of 88 cents for offers.
Conventional gasoline prices in both cities were unchanged late at 74/75 cents a gallon.
CARB gasoline sold for 79.50 cents a gallon, a 0.25 cent-fall from deals done yesterday. A paper deal for March was reported done at 80 cents.
Prices for CARB were lower after the American Petroleum Institute Tuesday reported West Coast gasoline inventories rose 612,000 barrels last week.
